title: F1 in Azerbaijan: That was almost a close-run thing
gist: Race recap of the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix: George Russell won for Mercedes despite a late turbo failure letting Red Bull's Verstappen close to 0.2s, while championship leader Antonelli recovered only to fifth. Gitlin highlights 2026 hybrid rule side-effects (11-12s battery deployment, locked gear ratios hurting McLaren), Ferrari leadership intrigue around Horner, toxic fan abuse, and Williams' overdue weight-fix chassis.

insights.claim: Under 2026 F1 rules, the hybrid power units can store only enough battery energy for about 11-12 seconds of full electric power, with the electric motor supplying almost half of the cars' 1,005 hp, so straight-line speeds at Baku were notably lower than a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Energy-storage limits reshape racing product and showcase battery/hybrid technology constraints.
insights.quote: can only store enough energy in their batteries for around 11–12 seconds of full power

insights.claim: Teams must declare all eight gear ratios plus final drive before the 2026 season with only one change allowed, which left McLaren's short gearing making it the second-slowest car in a straight line at Baku.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Locked-in engineering choices create persistent track-specific winners and losers.
insights.quote: you have to declare all eight ratios (plus the final drive) before the start of the year

insights.claim: F1 withheld speed and battery state-of-charge graphics on the main straight despite showing them elsewhere, which the author calls inconsistent with CEO Stefano Domenicali's claim that viewers don't care how cars are driven.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Suggests the series is managing perception of the unpopular energy-limited rules.
insights.locator: Notably, F1 did not show us

insights.claim: Red Bull's V6 engine is the most powerful in the field, placing both its cars highly, with Verstappen finishing within two-tenths of Russell after Russell suffered a late turbocharger failure.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Power-unit competitiveness is the key differentiator under the new regulations.
insights.quote: Red Bull’s V6 engine is the most powerful in the field

insights.claim: Ferrari's Monza engine upgrade failed to close the gap, ending realistic title hopes and fueling lobbying to replace team boss Fred Vasseur with former Red Bull chief Christian Horner.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Leadership instability at Ferrari affects the team's commercial and sponsor narrative.
insights.quote: any realistic title hopes have evaporated

insights.claim: Williams, which sacrificed its 2025 car to focus on 2026, produced a car up to 70 lbs (32 kg) overweight; new chassis arriving at Baku finally put it under the 765 kg limit and yielded a point for Sainz.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Shows how rule-change bets can backfire for teams despite long lead time.
insights.quote: it was massively overweight, by as much as 70 lbs (32 kg)

insights.claim: George Russell led from start to finish from a pole nearly a second clear, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashed in Q1, started 16th, and finished fifth.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Mercedes has the season's best car, keeping its constructor dominance intact.

insights.claim: F1 moved the Baku race a day earlier to avoid clashing with Azerbaijan's celebration of its war with Armenia, which the author frames as a continuation of Ecclestone-era controversy.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Geopolitical host-country entanglements remain a reputational risk for F1's calendar.

insights.claim: Franco Colapinto's crash taking out teammate Gasly and Norris came amid Argentine fans' online abuse and death threats, with Alpine boss Flavio Briatore having threatened to cut Colapinto's media appearances; the author notes a similar pattern got Augustin Canapino fired from IndyCar.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Fan toxicity is a growing brand-safety issue for teams and sponsors.
